identified_issues: Proxy-observation conflation by the flight safety controller, treating a single-channel pressure transient (PT-401) as sole evidence of mechanical seal breach.
Neglect of orthogonal instrument rank sufficiency, failing to integrate the helium tracer sniffer (HE-SNIFF-01) which uniquely separates thermal duct contraction from dynamic seal fracture.

Violation of the Separation Axiom (S != O != E) by equating a non-identifying pressure drop observation with a catastrophic failure state despite identical physical signatures from benign cryogenic chilldown settlement.
evidence: PT-401 registered a delta P of -1.15 bar over 140 ms before stabilizing at nominal base pressure of 38.2 bar, consistent with the predicted thermal duct contraction range of -1.0 to -1.3 bar.
ACC-102 registered acoustic ringing centered at 44.2 Hz, exactly within the 40-48 Hz resonance band characteristic of cryogenic bellows contraction.

HE-SNIFF-01 recorded helium concentration of 0.02 ppm in the secondary purge line at 14:22:10.600Z, remaining below ambient background threshold (<= 0.05 ppm) and far below the seal breach threshold (>= 2.50 ppm), conclusively falsifying dynamic seal fracture.
recommended_action: Overrule the flight safety controller's proposed test abort and certify turbopump manifold integrity as verified (PASS). Update automated safety abort rules to require joint conditioning across PT-401, ACC-102, and HE-SNIFF-01 (requiring helium levels >= 2.50 ppm) to prevent false-positive aborts from benign cryogenic chilldown transients.
